raw_response:
I’m 63 now, and with only two people in the house and some labor going off-farm, I can’t spread myself too thin. So this year I’ll still keep wheat-maize on most of the land because it is the steadiest, and I know this rotation well. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece, mainly to spread risk and keep some cash income, but I won’t put too much area into it because cotton needs more watching and more picking labor. Water I have from the well, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate blindly. For wheat already in the field, I’ll manage it through harvest with one more nitrogen topdress and 1-2 irrigations depending on rain. After wheat comes off, I’ll plant maize right away on the same land with simple tillage so I don’t miss the window. Cotton I’ll plant in late April with a moderate fertilizer rate, not too heavy, because if I spend too much on inputs at my age and with limited labor, it is hard to get that money back. I usually stay a bit on the safe side: enough fertilizer so the crop doesn’t look weak, enough water at key stages, and pesticides only when I really see a problem.
